review_scope: Independent quad/object fragment only. Dispatch/copy/compute workers and allocation/free review are supplied separately and must be merged before whole-program acceptance.

c6_background.notes: C6 is the source/design background only. This review used the returned C43 compiler assembly and actual production-object disassembly; it makes no complete machine-code identity claim against C6.

quad_helpers.stack_frame_description: Fixed 752-byte frame, no ADDVL scalable stack allocation. General-register saves and numerous scalar/pointer temporaries occupy the frame. STP/LDP d8,d9 at sp+112 and d10,d11 at sp+128 are callee-saved low-64-bit SIMD ABI preservation, outside the arithmetic loops; they are not accumulator spills.
quad_helpers.spill_notes: Whole helper, including all out-of-line labels after the normal return, has no LDR/STR Z or Q, no predicate spill, and no LD1W/ST1W to stack storage. Actual vector stores at .L363 are the 16 output vectors. Their base pointers are recovered through the scalar pointer bundle at sp+552..576. The only stack-address aliases formed are x8=sp+552, frame x29=sp+16, and x0=sp+552; the bundle is accessed with integer STP/LDP, then loaded external destination pointers are used by ST1W. Other stack loads in stage setup are integer input/kernel address or loop-state reloads.
quad_helpers.transition_spill_review: Read every instruction from function label through .size, including the seven stage setup/exit sections, .L338 one-column loop, straight-line remaining-column paths under .L339/.L344/.L348/.L353/.L357/.L361, all .L335/.L373/.L374/.L393/.L394/.L396 initialization branches, .L350 row advance, .L363 output stores and horizontal-block advance, and .L332/.L392/.L395 fallback edges. Accumulators remain in Z registers across all phases. Integer address temporaries are saved/reloaded at transitions, but no vector value is spilled. No live output accumulator crosses a helper call; stores or the no-main-block path precede fallback calls.
quad_helpers.tail_and_fallback_review: Entry kh<=3 branches .L332 to rowtriple followed by prefix for row 3. Width below CNTB (4*svcntw float outputs) uses .L392/.L334 and .L395. After complete 4VL blocks, .L395 calls rowtriple for rows 0..2 at column i and then tail-branches to prefix for row 3 at the same column, with ow-i remaining. ABI restore order is valid on main, fallback and tail-branch paths. Original q0/q1 arithmetic ordering remains, while actual GCC remaining-column paths can contain up to two sequential single-column copies guarded by kw; these are not an additional paired-vector read.

production_object_correspondence.method: Read the remote-produced objdump text of production-conv2d.o. Matched all 1554 non-padding compiler instructions, operands and the 43 internal label targets in order; this was lightweight text inspection, not a local assembler/disassembler execution. All seven loop address ranges are recorded above. The only spelling/alias adjustments beyond punctuation/numeric formatting are PTRUE p0.b,all shown as PTRUE p0.b, 32-bit AND -2 shown as 0xfffffffe, and UXTW x19,w9 shown as MOV w19,w9. Four helper branches/calls resolve to rowtriple at 0x2684 and prefix at 0x3e4.
production_object_correspondence.production_flags_evidence: raw/build-production.log actual + gcc command builds conv2d.c with -O3 -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off -mcpu=generic -fopenmp -DCONV_BLOCK=32 -DCONV_KERNEL_UNROLL=2 -c; raw/build-assembly.log has the same code-generation flags and -S. No instrumentation or probe include is present in either command.

fma_scan_scope: Entire returned conv2d-sve.s and production-conv2d-objdump.log, including all helpers and dispatch workers. Checked fused families fmla/fmls/fmad/fmsb/fnmla/fnmls/fnmad/fnmsb/fmadd/fmsub/fnmadd/fnmsub/fmlal/fmlal2/fmlsl/fmlsl2/fmmla; both counts are zero. This whole-source arithmetic scan does not replace the separate dispatch/copy-path control-flow review.

dispatch_functions.role: New OMP static row-copy worker, invoked only after successful allocation.
dispatch_functions.stack_frame_description: 64 bytes. Scalar ABI saves x19..x24 and x29/x30; no SVE/NEON stack state or vector arithmetic.
dispatch_functions.spill_notes: No vector stack loads/stores or vector accumulator spills in this worker. Scalar callee saves preserve copy pointers across memcpy.
dispatch_functions.copy_path_notes: Capture fields [0,8] are original input/stride, [16,24] allocated destination/padded stride, [32] original width*4 bytes, [40] input height. Both strides shift by two once. Each .L4 iteration calls memcpy(dst,src,row_bytes), advances source by original stride bytes and destination by padded stride bytes using memcpy return=dst. Padding is not copied or read by the worker. Object memcpy is at0x80, increments0x84/0x88.
dispatch_functions.control_flow_notes: omp_get_num_threads/thread_num produce quotient/remainder static partition of inputHeight; .L2 grants one extra row to early threads, .L5 computes nonoverlapping contiguous first/end rows and exits empty partitions. .L4 copies exactly those rows; join occurs on parent GOMP_parallel return. No malloc/free or compute helper in worker.

dispatch_functions.role: Legacy output-row static worker for the public non-SVE branch, with inline NEON tiles 32/16/8/4/2/1 and preserved conditional prefix branch.
dispatch_functions.stack_frame_description: 368 bytes. Scalar ABI x19..x28/x29/x30; d8..d15 saved at sp+96..159 and restored once on worker exit. sp+160..239 stores row/loop state. sp+240..367 is the local output tile array, reused for 32-,16-,8-float tails.
dispatch_functions.spill_notes: No observed non-ABI vector reload from stack and no register-pressure accumulator spill/reload pair in kernel loops. Distinguish 4 STP/4 LDP instructions for ABI d8..d15 from 14 static STR Q instructions that materialize completed tile arrays after the kh backedge: lines1214..1235 (8),1491..1500 (4),2138/2141 (2). Those Q values are then read by GPR LDP and copied to final output at1238..1256,1503..1513,2144..2149. They are real stack traffic, explicitly not a claim of a stack-free program.
dispatch_functions.copy_path_notes: No calls to malloc, memcpy, free or copy interposition. The local tile-array copy is output materialization and is distinct from the new whole-input copy. Public non-SVE capture passes original input/stride and use_sve=0, so the retained .L68 conv_sve_prefix branch is not reached from that public branch.
dispatch_functions.control_flow_notes: Quotient/remainder OMP partitions output rows. .L75 forms row input/output bases; .L69/.L132/.L118/.L106/.L96/.L86 dispatch descending width tiles32/16/8/4/2/1. Per-row .L84 increments original input stride and global output ow. Hot kh loops retain FP values in registers; materialization follows their exits, then advances output tile. Remaining cold kw-unroll branches at end of function jump back into the same arithmetic flow. Object confirms 368-byte prologue0x8a4, ABI stores0x9ac..0x9b8, tile Q stores0xf74..0xfac/0x1384..0x139c/0x1c18..0x1c20 and GPR copies following each; conditional prefix call0x14d0. Only other calls are OMP thread queries.

dispatch_functions.role: SVE static group-of-four compute worker with quad/triple/pair/prefix remainder dispatch.
dispatch_functions.stack_frame_description: 160 bytes. Scalar ABI x19..x28/x29/x30, scalar loop/capture state sp+124..159, outgoing helper arguments sp+0/sp+8. No vector stack state in this worker; helpers have separate frames.
dispatch_functions.spill_notes: No FP/SVE instructions or vector spills in the dispatcher. Scalar kernel pointer at sp+136 is preserved across helper calls; outgoing destination/ow arguments are not vector spills.
dispatch_functions.copy_path_notes: Captured input and independent stride are either original or successful copied/padded values, selected by conv2d before entering. Output base and ow remain global. Input advances by4*sve_stride floats, output by4*ow floats; no malloc/memcpy/free occurs here.
dispatch_functions.control_flow_notes: Static quotient/remainder partition of ceil(oh/4) groups, first row=4*group. Remaining>3 selects quad (.s .L402/object call0x4ffc); remaining3 selects triple(.L403/0x507c),2 pair(.L404/0x5048),1 prefix(.L408/0x4f94). Destination row1/2/3 offsets derive from global ow, never padded stride. .L405 advances four rows and exits at group end; no overlapping output groups.

dispatch_functions.role: Public validation/HWCAP dispatch, checked optional allocation, two sequential OMP regions, final release.
dispatch_functions.stack_frame_description: 176 bytes. Scalar ABI x19..x28/x29/x30, temporary padded-stride/capture pointers around sp+96, captured OMP structures sp+120..171. No FP/SVE stack operands.
dispatch_functions.spill_notes: No vector spills. Scalar saved registers preserve original input/stride across malloc and selected input/stride across copy GOMP; nonnull allocation is kept in x21 until compute returns.
dispatch_functions.copy_path_notes: Actual eligibility .L431 computes odd 16-float-line stride, compares it with original, checks product and512MiB cap, then .L432 malloc. NULL jumps .L416 while x26/x28 remain original. Success captures old input/stride and new pointer/stride for copy worker, replaces x26/x28 with copied/padded values, calls copy GOMP, then .L416 compute GOMP. Only afterwards does nonnull x21 tail-branch free; zero skips free.
dispatch_functions.control_flow_notes: Invalid kernel dimensions return before subtraction or HWCAP. getauxval(16), TBZbit22 selects public non-SVE worker .L415. SVE gate requires width>=64,kh>=4,oh>=4. Gate/stride/cap failure uses original SVE path. Object invalid tests0x5094..0x50e0, HWCAP0x5110..0x5118, eligibility0x511c..0x5128/0x51e8..0x5228, malloc0x5230 and NULL branch0x5240, copy GOMP0x5274 and branch back0x527c, compute GOMP0x5164, free tail0x5188. Non-SVE path0x518c..0x51d0 calls fn2 with use_sve zero and never allocates.

copy_path_review.eligibility_and_overflow: Actual public function first enforces positive kh/kw and kh<=height,kw<=width, making dimensions positive int32. SVE bit22 and width>=64/kh>=4/oh>=4 precede allocation. .L431 add15/and-16/orr16 computes ((width+15)/16 |1)*16 floats and equality disables copy. Maximum padded stride is2^31+16 for positive int32 width; add15, width*4 and height*padded_stride are therefore representable in64-bit size_t (product<2^63). GCC removes source guards proven redundant under those ranges; retained compare toSIZE_MAX/4 precedes shift2 and compare to536870912. Failure paths preserve original input/stride. This is static bound/control-flow proof, not a huge-allocation dynamic test.
copy_path_review.malloc_and_null_fallback: One malloc in public .L432 after all gates; object0x5230. x21 receives result, cbz x0 at0x5240 reaches shared compute .L416 without rewriting original x26=input/x28=stride. No copy region is launched and x21=0 skips free on this path. Success rewrites selected pointers only after NULL branch.
copy_path_review.row_memcpy_and_stride: Copy capture stores original input/original stride and allocated output/padded stride separately, plus original row_bytes=width*4 and full inputHeight. Worker0 static row partition is disjoint, uses exact row_bytes once per assigned row and independent strides in bytes. No padding bytes feed the convolution: helper logical widths and kw stay unchanged while only row stride changes. Actual memcpy source is never output, and input/kernel remain readonly.
copy_path_review.compute_and_free_order: Copy GOMP_parallel completes at public0x5274 before branch0x527c to .L416/compute0x5164; compute returns before cbz allocation and tail free0x5188. OMP region return is the join/barrier semantics here; no standalone barrier instruction is invented. All worker helpers finish before the shared input copy is freed, once per successful invocation; no persistent allocation/state.
copy_path_review.noncopy_and_non_sve_fallback: Disabled gate, unchanged padded stride, cap failure and malloc NULL all reach original SVE compute with original stride and no free. HWCAP-not-SVE directly captures original input/kernel/output/stride and use_sve=0 for worker2, bypassing all allocation/copy/free logic. Invalid dimensions return immediately. Worker2 actual machine code and stack traffic were reviewed statically; the six H configurations do not provide forced non-SVE dynamic coverage.

dispatch_review_notes.review_scope: Actual returned production assembly: complete public conv2d and all three conv2d OMP workers, with corresponding production object disassembly. Quad arithmetic is reviewed in the independent quad fragment, not duplicated here.
dispatch_review_notes.production_identity_notes: build-production.log actual + gcc argv compiles conv2d.c alone with GCC 10.3.1, generic, -O3 -fno-fast-math -ffp-contract=off -fopenmp and original macros; it does not compile instrumented_candidate.c or include copy-probe interposition. The .s SHA is calculated once here from the returned file; object SHA is taken from returned production-object-sha256.txt.
dispatch_review_notes.object_mapping_limit: The returned objdump is of a relocatable production object. Some adrp/add symbol-address placeholders show zero before link; worker identity is read from the named .s relocations and matched object instructions/control flow, not inferred from misleading unresolved zero addresses. No claim that .s text proves whole-program byte identity with C6.
dispatch_review_notes.dynamic_coverage_limit: All six H configurations execute on SVE hardware (VL16/32/64, threads1/4). Legacy non-SVE worker inspection below is static actual-machine-code review, not an additional dynamically forced non-SVE test. 512 MiB and size_t extremes are static-only coverage.
dispatch_review_notes.review_conclusion: No blocker found in the actual production dispatch/copy control flow or object correspondence. This fragment does not assert whole-quad completion, benchmark performance, promotion, huge-size dynamic coverage, or whole-program no-stack/no-spill.

merge_notes: Combined completed independent reviews of the same returned production artifacts; compiler_version normalized from the dispatch banner to 10.3.1. Original fragments remain unchanged.
